text:
Alex: Heads up — started seeing higher error rates from Tempo exporter for tenant 'acme' right after yesterday's routing change. Logs show `grpc: deadline exceeded` and `resource exhausted`. Anyone else? :eyes:
Maya: Yep, noticed the alarms. This looks correlated with the new fanout policy that duplicates OTLP to both Honeycomb and Tempo. Small tenants get queued then TTL-evicted.
Chris: We did change the otelcol pipeline — per-tenant fanout + exporter-level backpressure. Tempo is gRPC, Honeycomb is HTTP/batched. Batching mismatch + bursty spans could be triggering backpressure upstream.
Jenn: Tempo ingesters return `resource exhausted` when their per-ingester queue spikes. We saw a large synthetic trace payload in the ingress tests (huge span count), which amplifies the problem.
Alex: Important question: do we prioritize latency SLOs (fail fast) or durability (buffer & retry)? For product traces, latency matters. For compliance traces maybe durability.
Rory: Routing only to Honeycomb as a temporary mitigation isn't harmless — Honeycomb doesn't preserve some low-level span pointer relationships for very wide traces, so the Trace UI can be truncated. That would break some customer expectations.
Chris: Proposal: small canary rollout. 5% of traffic fanout to both honeycomb+tempo (for verification), 95% keep the default route. Add exporter-side adaptive buffering (tune `max_queued_bytes`, `max_concurrent_requests`) and a drop policy for oversized items. Also emit per-tenant queue_depth metric to the Console.
Jenn: Also need a dedicated dashboard: exporter_5xx_rate, exporter_queue_bytes, tempo_ingester_throttle_count, and per-tenant sample_rate. Tag by tenant_id + route.
Alex: +1. I'll also put a temporary burst quota on 'acme' to limit peak. That buys time while we tune backpressure.
Maya: I'll open a PR with the otelcol config changes (will include `queued_retry_on_failure=true`, a `drop_after_bytes` policy, and honeycomb batch window tweaks). Will add dashboard panels in the same PR. /cc @eng-sre :wave:
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for otelcol fanout v2 — 50/50 split for the selected 5% tenants. Link: https://deploys.redwood/123
Rory: If we're running a canary, set the TTL eviction lower (30s) so queues don't grow unobserved. Long TTLs will fill heap in the fanout path.
Jenn: I'll add an alert: `tempo_exporter_5xx_rate > 1%` for 5m -> page eng-sre and notify `#incidents`. Also add a silent slack alert for queue_depth > threshold so oncall can watch.
Chris: Good. Let's reconvene in 2 hours after metrics stabilize. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
